title: Private min pack: initial Grafana provisioning framework (folders, naming, variable templates)
author: Sergio Costa
body: Title: Private min pack: initial Grafana provisioning framework (folders, naming, variable templates). Context: This PR lays down the baseline structure for the Private Observability Minimum Pack dashboards so we can ship a versioned, repeatable set of Grafana assets across VPC + on-prem installs without bespoke per-customer work. This is intentionally “scaffolding first”: folders, naming conventions, datasource contract, and templating variables that subsequent dashboards can plug into. Linked: ENG-2841 (repo structure + provisioning). Scope: Grafana provisioning only (dashboards + folder layout + variable templates). No alert rules in this PR (those land in PR-322+). Changes: (1) Repository structure + conventions: Introduces a top-level `private-min-pack/` module with subfolders for dashboards and provisioning assets. Establishes naming conventions for dashboards, folders, and UIDs to keep upgrades stable (UIDs are deterministic and do not embed environment-specific strings). Adds `CONTRIBUTING.md` notes on dashboard review (avoid secrets, avoid high-cardinality vars, keep panel queries portable). (2) Grafana provisioning skeleton: Adds `grafana/provisioning/dashboards/private-min-pack.yaml` with a dedicated folder ("Redwood Private / Minimum Pack") and a file-based provider that loads dashboards from a mounted path. Adds an explicit datasource name contract for Prometheus (`PROM_DS=Prometheus`) and a placeholder hook for Loki/other log sources (off by default). (3) Variable templates: Adds a small set of standard templating variables to be reused across dashboards: `$cluster`, `$namespace`, `$release`, `$instance`, `$tenant`, `$route`, `$model`. Variables are designed to be safe-by-default: tenant/route/model are opt-in and only appear if the corresponding labels are present; defaults fall back to “all” and queries constrain label matchers to prevent explosion. (4) Lint/validation helpers: Adds a `make grafana-validate` target that checks JSON validity, enforces UID presence, and ensures the folder/provider file paths remain consistent. Adds a CI job entry to run the validation on PRs (lightweight, no Grafana container required). Notes: This PR does not include actual dashboards beyond a “placeholder” dashboard used to validate provisioning end-to-end. The follow-up PRs (319/320/321/324/325) will add the real dashboards using these conventions. Testing: - `make grafana-validate` - `make test` (repo unit checks) - Manual: imported placeholder dashboard into a local Grafana (10.4.x) with Prometheus datasource named `Prometheus` and verified templating variables resolve without errors when optional labels are missing. Files / areas changed (high level): - grafana/provisioning/dashboards/private-min-pack.yaml (new) - grafana/dashboards/private-min-pack/_template.variables.json (new) - grafana/dashboards/private-min-pack/zz_placeholder.private-min-pack.json (new) - scripts/grafana_validate.py (new) - Makefile (updated) - .github/workflows/ci.yml (updated) - docs/CONTRIBUTING.md (updated) Illustrative snippet (provisioning provider): apiVersion: 1 providers: - name: "redwood-private-min-pack" orgId: 1 folder: "Redwood Private / Minimum Pack" type: file disableDeletion: false updateIntervalSeconds: 30 options: path: /var/lib/grafana/dashboards/private-min-pack. Commits: - "Create private-min-pack directory layout + conventions" - "Add Grafana dashboard provider + folder naming" - "Add standard dashboard variables template" - "Add grafana-validate script + CI wiring" - "Docs: dashboard guidelines (UIDs, variables, cardinality)" Review conversation (highlights): - Allison Grant: “Please document the UID policy explicitly. We’ve been bitten by Grafana recreating dashboards as duplicates on upgrade.” Sergio: “Added deterministic UID guidance + validation check requiring UID field.” - Sean Gallagher: “Default variables should not include tenant/model unless the label contract is in place; otherwise operators see broken dropdowns.” Sergio: “Updated variable queries to use `label_values(up{job=~"redwood.*"}, tenant)` pattern with `or` fallback; also ensured dashboards don’t fail rendering when variables are empty.” - Nadia Rahman: “Be careful about route/model label cardinality. Avoid regex `.*` on high-cardinality labels by default.” Sergio: “Template uses `allValue` only for low-cardinality vars; tenant/route/model remain multi-select but not used in base panels unless explicitly referenced.” - Bruno Silva: “Installer will mount dashboards; please keep the path stable and avoid relying on Grafana-side folder creation via API.” Sergio: “Provider is file-based with a single stable mount path; no API calls needed.” CI / checks: - build: pass - lint: pass - grafana-validate: pass - unit: pass. Merge: Squash merged into `main` on 2025-02-11. Follow-ups: PR-319 (gateway/service overview dashboard), PR-320 (runtime performance dashboard), PR-321 (GPU saturation), PR-324 (control plane), PR-325 (install health).
